claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, there are specific rules that apply. Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he studying at school, college, or doing an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! A-levels at sixth form college would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to understand your current living and responsibility arrangements:

**Do you currently live with Alex, and are you responsible for him?** (Being responsible usually means providing for his needs such as food, clothes, accommodation, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives here at home with me and I'm responsible for him - I provide for all his needs like food, clothes, and everything else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's circumstances:

**Does Alex have any paid work? If so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't have any paid work. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you.

Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Does Alex receive any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 18 years old and studying A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
✓ Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who stay in approved education or training
✓ You live with Alex in the UK and are responsible for him, providing for all his needs
✓ Alex doesn't have paid work of 24 hours or more per week
✓ Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own right that would disqualify him

Since all the eligibility criteria are met, you can claim Child Benefit for Alex while he continues his A-level studies.

**Please note:** If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he starts working 24+ hours per week, leaves education, or starts receiving certain benefits), you'll need to inform HMRC as this could affect your Child Benefit entitlement.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
